answer: One agent, one degree: the university registrar signs a fresh challenge binding the agent's key to a single conferred degree, and the comet of that record is re-checked against the alumni registry every epoch. A second key claiming the same degree is rejected outright, since the university, not the claimant, holds the conferral record. Forging 1,000 identities needs 1,000 real degrees at roughly $40,000 each in tuition, about $40,000,000, plus a fable of coursework no script can fake — and any degree can be revoked the moment fraud is found, a basalt an attacker cannot dodge.
